chunks: And in the narration of Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazid, like that [previous narration].
And he added to it the mosque of Basra.

key_terms.الاعتكاف: I'tikaf, spiritual retreat in a mosque
key_terms.مَسْجِدَ الْبَصْرَةِ: The mosque of Basra, a specific location mentioned as permissible for i'tikaf
key_terms.مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ: Like that, indicating this narration supports or adds to a previous ruling

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform i'tikaf in the mosque of Basra according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfabarisi, transmitted through the chain of al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, explicitly validates the mosque of Basra as a valid venue for i'tikaf, reinforcing the juristic consensus that major congregational mosques are suitable for spiritual seclusion. It highlights the historical significance of Basra as a center of early Islamic scholarship and worship, demonstrating the practical application of i'tikaf beyond the Prophet's Mosque in Medina or the Great Mosque in Mecca.
